narrative:
The model estimated a 57.4% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That means failure was judged slightly more likely than passing, so the application was denied based on that prediction—not because failure was treated as certain. Your gender and race did not drive this decision.

The strongest influence was your first-year class-rank decile: it was 1, far below the average of 6 among accepted students. That low early standing pushed the prediction most strongly toward bar-exam failure. The third strongest factor, your third-year decile of 2 versus an accepted average of 5.79, also pushed toward failure, though less strongly. In contrast, your undergraduate GPA of 3.40 was above the accepted average of 3.23; this was the second most important factor and it pushed toward passing, partially offsetting the class-rank concerns.

To improve a future application, ask admissions for feedback and address the early academic record directly. Consider whether additional upper-level coursework, a stronger LSAT retake, or a delayed application with documented improvement would demonstrate readiness. Provide context for any early difficulties and show an upward trend; the model is not a final judgment, and a stronger recent record could change the outcome.
